turns.input: Korvin gives Nicco a pair of leather boots.
turns.narration:
Korvin's gruff frame halts an arm's length away, those perceptive eyes sweeping Nicco's worn footwear with the quick assessment of a man who sizes up livestock and laborers alike. He reaches into a coarse-woven sack at his side and produces a pair of leather boots, scarred from use but solid, the soles still thick enough to last.

"These'll hold you better than whatever you're walking on now," he says, voice rough as gravel, the cadence of West District warehouses still clinging to his words. He extends them not quite into Nicco's hands, holding back that final inch, watching for the reaction of a customer who's being handed something unasked-for. "Fair trade for a man who keeps his own tower and looks like he forgot to pack proper."

turns.input:
Thanks *he said to them, after which he decides to give them back the boots*
You'll need them more than me
turns.narration:
Korvin's small eyes narrow slightly—appraising, not offended. "Keep 'em," he says, rough voice flat with the finality of someone who has already decided a transaction's end. "Not a loan. Bought cheap, sold cheaper, doesn't matter to me." He doesn't reach for the returned boots, hands staying loose at his sides, those damaged knuckles catching the daylight. "You own this heap of stone now. Walk around inside in your stockings, that's your foolishness. But step outside, you look like a mark."

He glances past Nicco toward the tower's main entrance, then back, the hook of his nose casting a small shadow. "Or don't. None of my concern what you do with free leather." A shrug moves through his compact shoulders, the gesture of a man who has learned not to press where no profit lies. He waits, watching to see whether Nicco will persist in the return or let the matter drop.
